threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 bus is a reliable option after 10 PM. Good luck with that, mate.
Spotted a guy arguing with the driver because he wouldn’t let his pet parrot ride. Parrot was just chilling on his shoulder, not a care in the world.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh pretzels from the corner bakery at sunrise while the late-night party crowd still winds down. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a park where a bunch of grown-ups bring their kids to play while they sip on craft beer from the nearby bar.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how quick they get off the train at Civic Center when there's a hint of smoke—everyone else just freezes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy balancing on a skateboard, juggling oranges while waiting for the 38. Classic San Francisco multitasking, right? Never a dull moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think it's all about Gaudí, but the actual charm’s in the little squares where locals gather for vermut on Sunday afternoons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the lack of tap water in most restaurants – locals just order a 'copa d'aigua' and carry on.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look surprised when the bus is late. Locals know 10 minutes is basically on time, but you’re still figuring that out.
Caught a bloke on the 59 last night offering his seat to a statue. True story. The statue was still covered in pigeon guano. London nights, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh kebabs mixing with the sound of a late night saxophonist outside my window made me realize this place has a heartbeat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a silent disco in an abandoned factory. Headphones on, you dance among graffiti and echoes of the past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local orders a burrito at La Taqueria and asks for it 'half and half' without blinking. Tourists always fumble at the counter.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 bus today; a guy serenaded us with a ukulele. At least he played 'San Francisco'—the one moment of joy amid the usual chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think the 'poble' in Gràcia means village, but it’s really more about the spirit—community over convenience.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they ask for a ‘café con leche’ in the afternoon—locals stick to ‘café amb llet’ after 12.
